name: Document Picture-in-Picture
plain: Opens a small always-on-top window containing any HTML.
meaning: Floats custom page content above other windows (video call controls, timers). A page can keep a floating surface visible while you work elsewhere, so it can also be abused for fake UI.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; needs a gesture. The floating window shows the origin and is closable.

chrome_android.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

limits.headline: Can open a small floating window with its own content after you click
limits.user_action: You tap a button such as Pop out or Mini player.
can: Open a small always-on-top window with any page content, such as a timer, chat or video controls
Keep it showing while you use other windows
Update what it shows as time passes
cannot: Open it without a click, tap or keypress
Hide which site it belongs to, since the window shows the site name
Open it on phones or in Firefox and Safari
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Firefox, Safari and phones do not have it.

story.what_it_is: Opens a small always on top window that can hold any page content, not just video.

marketing.name: Document Picture-in-Picture
marketing.pitch: Chrome says it lets sites pop out any content into an always on top window, like video calls or timers.

story.for_you: A small window floats above your other apps. It may show a video call, a game, a timer or notes. It stays while you work in another tab.
story.for_makers: It keeps people inside the product when they switch tasks. A video call or a game keeps going on screen. That means longer sessions and fewer missed moments.

use_cases.example: A video call keeps the faces and the mute button in a small floating window while you open a spreadsheet.
A browser puzzle or trivia game floats the timer and question while you read notes in another tab.
A live sports score and chat float over your work so you can follow a match.
A timer or a notes box floats over every tab while you work.
A music site pops out the playlist and controls, not only a video frame.
An ad supported video player keeps a small window open so it keeps getting watch time.
A language app keeps flashcards floating beside a lecture video.
